research_rationale: Executive Order 7747 of November 20, 1937 establishes the water around San Clemente Island, California, out to three hundred yards from low-water mark as a defensive sea area under section 44 of the Criminal Code (18 U.S.C. 96), restricts navigation within it to craft authorized by the Secretary of the Navy, and subjects violators to legal penalties. The held text is the Federal Register print as machine-extracted from the official PDF (2 FR 2947) with closing number [No. 7747]; the three paragraphs are one scheme and the dossier holds them as one clause. The order continued, as amended by Executive Order 8536 (1940-09-06, extent changed to one nautical mile and the area named) and restated by Executive Order 9787 (1946-10-05, restated to read as follows with changed extents), until Executive Order 9894, signed 1947-09-23, ordered that the San Clemente Island Naval Defensive Sea Area, established by 7747 as amended by 8536 and 9787, be discontinued. Amendments and the restatement are later events recorded with before-and-after text under the strike-and-insert ruling, not ends; the end is the express discontinuance. The packet's number-citation search lists the held later texts that name 7747 (8536, 9787 and 9894).

Executive Order 8536 and Executive Order 9787 amend and restate the order and keep the defensive sea area in being, so they are later events and not ends; the first instrument that ends the area is Executive Order 9894, which names 7747 as amended by 8536 and 9787.
scope_check: The order has three paragraphs (establishment of the area, restriction of navigation, penalty); all three depend on the existence of the defensive sea area, and 9894 discontinues the area, so they end together. One clause is retained.
independent_command_check: The navigation restriction and the penalty paragraph operate only within the area defined in the first paragraph; no command in the order operates independently of the area. savings_check: Executive Order 9894 states no saving or transfer; recorded as none after the packet's bounded search.

research_rationale: Executive Order 7845 of March 21, 1938 prescribes regulations on annual leave for civilian officers and employees of the United States, the District of Columbia and covered corporations under section 7 of the act of March 14, 1936 (49 Stat. 1161). The held text is the Federal Register print as machine-extracted from the official PDF (3 FR 715 to 717). The dossier inventory is corrected in four ways: an enacting-paragraph clause is added; section 9 and section 19(e) are each split at a page break so the Federal Register page header and table of contents are not carried inside a clause; section 19(e) is separated from section 19(f), which the machine segmentation merged because the held text prints (f) as "if)"; and Part headings are trimmed from the ends of sections 1(i) and 18. Sections 20 through 22 are retained. Executive Order 8384, signed 1940-03-29, states that it supersedes Executive Orders No. 7845, No. 7879 and No. 8226 and is effective as of March 2, 1940, so the continuing regulatory clauses end on 1940-03-02; its sections 6 and 9 are effective as of July 1, 1936 for leave adjustments, which is disclosed for sections 6 and 9. Section 20 (ratification and revocation of inconsistent regulations), section 21 (effective date and supersession of Executive Order 7409) and section 22 (publication) are one-time commands exhausted by performance, recorded with their performance dates rather than the later supersession. Section 6 was restated by Executive Order 7879 (1938-05-09) and section 15 by Executive Order 8226 (1939-08-24); both are later events with before-and-after text, not ends.
